incident-bot: INCIDENT OPENED 2071234567 - sev:sev2 - summary: KV-cache reuse causing stale cross-request values under heavy paging/continuous-batching. Alerting on error-rate spike and content-mismatch reports.

Alice K: seeing lots of customer reports that completions are repeating fragments incorrectly when responses are paged. Also a jump in runtime errors in the serving logs.

Ben R: is this the same pattern as last month? paging + large batch sizes?

Carmen L: different. This looks like kv-cache keys being used by the wrong request id after page boundary. I have a few traces where seq_offset for the KV page is wrong.

SRE Oncall: can you paste one of the traces?

Carmen L: here — logs (redacted):
```
[2026-11-02T09:12:34Z] req=abc123 page=2 kv_lookup key=tok_0 owner_req=abc123 owner_seq=512 found_seq=256 value_len=128
[2026-11-02T09:12:34Z] req=def456 page=1 kv_lookup key=tok_0 owner_req=def456 owner_seq=256 found_seq=256 value_len=128
[2026-11-02T09:12:34Z] req=abc123 continued with found_seq=256 -> mismatch -> incorrect tokens emitted
```

Carmen L: notice owner_req mismatches. Looks like a reuse path is not resetting owner metadata on a paged response.

Support Eng: We’ve had 3 enterprise customers report garbled completions and one escalated for incorrect PII redaction (false positive). Customer impact = wrong outputs + increased latency.

ML Oncall: this is bad. If the KV cache returns entries owned by a different request, outputs could leak across users. Need immediate mitigation.

Ben R: propose emergency mitigations: 1) disable KV_CACHE_REUSE flag globally 2) roll back any recent continuous-batching increase 3) enable per-request KV namespace tagging. Which can we do fastest?

SRE Oncall: disabling KV_CACHE_REUSE is just flipping a config on the runtime, we can push a hotfix in <10min. Rolling back batch config requires coordination with autoscaler — but we can set a temporary max_batch_size=1 for the affected pool to reduce reuse.

Alice K: do we know which pools are affected? Looks like us-east-gpu-pool and eu-west-batch.

deploy-bot: deploy starting - target: runtime-config/kv_disable_hotfix - user: SRE Oncall - roll: canary 5% -> 20% -> 100%

SRE Oncall: canary 5% live. Monitoring errors and latency.

Carmen L: also pushing a small runtime patch to ensure sequence_owner is validated on every KV read; if owner doesn't match, evict and fallback to compute. That can be slightly slower but safe.

Ben R: for immediate impact, do both: disable reuse + lower batching. Patch is for correctness and will be in next deploy.

Support Eng: I told customers we are rolling a mitigation now and will follow up in 30m with impact summary.

incident-bot: deploy status: canary OK -> stepping to 20% at 2071234585.

Alice K: after the initial flip, error-rate dropped by ~60% on the impacted pools, but there are still traces of stale owners for long-lived paged requests.

ML Oncall: how long are those long-lived streams? paging with >10 pages seems more likely. Could be a stale kv page retention bug.

Carmen L: confirmed. The bug is in the pager codepath where when we refill KV pages we reuse a KV slab without clearing owner_seq on the slab header. If a slab is reused between requests, owner_seq stays from previous request and later lookups match incorrectly.

Ben R: patch idea (pseudo):
```
if (slab.owner_id != current_request_id || slab.owner_seq != expected_seq) {
  slab.invalidate(); // evict stale metadata
  // fallback to recompute and repopulate
}
```

SRE Oncall: production hotfix already disabled reuse. I'm going to set max_batch_size=4 for eu-west and us-east pools to reduce pressure.

deploy-bot: runtime-config update complete at 2071234592 - max_batch_size set to 4 for pools: us-east, eu-west.

Support Eng: customers updated: two enterprises on standby for verification, no data exfil confirmed but outputs were incorrect for some requests.

Alice K: chasing a regression window — looks like a config bump to continuous-batching last night increased slab reuse aggressiveness. That exposed the slab clearing bug.

Carmen L: I have a local patch + unit tests that forcibly clear slab headers on free. Tests include simulated page interleaving and seq mismatch checks. Will open PR now.

Ben R: assign owners for follow-up: Carmen -> correctness patch + tests; ML Oncall -> verify model output regressions and generate a corpus of failing prompts; SRE Oncall -> validate rollback metrics and run a perf canary.

Carmen L: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/5421 (WIP) - adding extra validation and an eviction path.

SRE Oncall: perf impact from disabling reuse? token/sec dropped ~8% on those pools. Latency slightly up but still within SLO for most customers. We'll watch for cost impact.

ML Oncall: starting eval run with failing prompt corpus now. Will report false-positive/negative rates and sample diffs.

Support Eng: scheduled customer bridge at 2071234700 with two affected customers to walk through remediation.

Alice K: handoff: I'm going offline in 25min. Ben will take lead for coordination.

Ben R: taking lead. If anything spikes, page me. Running a full sweep for any other pools with high reuse counters.

incident-bot: NOTE: sev downgraded to sev3 at 2071234600 after mitigations initiated and no evidence of cross-customer leakage beyond incorrect tokens. Continue monitoring.

Carmen L: merged fix to canary branch with extra asserts. Will schedule full rollout after SRE signoff and bench results.

SRE Oncall: bench results: correctness patch has ~2% throughput regression in worst-case (large sequences), acceptable. Will coordinate rollout in maintenance window.

ML Oncall: eval shows majority of previously failing prompts now produce correct completions. A small number still differ — likely due to cached KV entries with partial funnels, but should be cleared with full rollout.

Support Eng: customers informed. One customer requested replay of the last 24h logs for their tenancy; legal & privacy signoff in progress.

Ben R: postmortem items: 1) stricter slab lifecycle tests 2) safety guard in runtime to evict on owner mismatch 3) telemetry: per-slab owner-change counters and alerts 4) change continuous-batching rollout guardrails (gradual per-pool) 5) runbook update for KV reuse disables.

Alice K: leaving notes in the incident doc. Thanks everyone.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED 2071234623 - reason: mitigations applied, patch ready for rollout, customers notified. Follow-up: postmortem in #postmortems in 48h.
